title: Multi-Domain Security for Tweaked-SR
summary: Tweaked-SR has a single-domain security theorem; it remains open to prove concurrent multi-domain security without encoding each domain size in the round keys.

formal_statement.body: The tweaked-SR constructed cipher is specified first for one fixed domain $[N_0]$; the unresolved extension is to prove security when an adversary may simultaneously encipher points from any number of domains $[N_0]$, for $N_0 \in \mathbb{N}$. In this multi-domain model, the round function and round keys may depend on the description of the current domain, but the conjecture is that the round keys need not encode $N_0$ itself. Establish this conjecture by extending the existing single-domain security theorem for tweaked-SR to the concurrent multi-domain setting.

scope.domain: Multi-domain security of the tweaked-SR cipher with round keys independent of the domain size.
assumptions: An adversary may simultaneously encipher points from any number of domains.
The round function may depend on the description of the current domain.
parameters: N₀: a natural number specifying the domain [N₀]
scope.unresolved_remainder: Extend the single-domain security theorem to concurrent domains while showing that round keys need not encode N₀.

progress.summary: The source presents domain-dependent round functions and keys as a way to support concurrent domains, then conjectures that the keys need not encode the domain size. It says a proof requires generalizing Theorem 5.
